question_text: During the recent hot season, the night time temperature of a certain room with closed windows in a house made of bricks was observed to be $35^\circ C$. A cooler opened the windows of the room for a few minutes at night and allowed the room to be filled with air person at $27^\circ C$ which was present outside the house. Once a quick time, the temperature of the room was observed to be $33^\circ C$. Which of the following reasons he had proposed to explain the observed effect is most unlikely to be accepted?

options.option_text: Low specific heat capacity of air
High specific heat capacity of bricks
Low thermal conductivity of brick walls
Collision of air molecules inside the room
Low specific heat capacity of air
